header: Date: 2025-05-28 | Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: 57m | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Silverline Head of ML), Priya Natarajan (SRE), Marcus Lee (Product)
summary: Redwood AE/SE demo of Eval & Quality Monitoring (Console + Optimize) focused on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons for Silverline Health's patient-summary assistant. Customer is interested in pilot to monitor hallucination/regressions, integration with CI, and data handling for PHI. Agreed next steps include pilot proposal, SOC2 + architecture docs, and sharing sample prompts/thresholds.
topics: Intro & qualification: current stack and goals
Demo: Console evals, prompt sets, A/B comparison UI
Telemetry: per-prompt metrics, token cost breakdown
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, uh we're gonna run through a focused demo on evals and quality monitoring, the console view, and how optimize ties into alerts and A B comparisons. Samira will drive the demo.
[00:16] Jordan Reyes: thanks Alex, appreciate it. we are primarily trying to catch hallucinations and things that drift after a model swap. our use case is the patient summary assistant, needs to avoid PHI leakage and maintain clinical accuracy.
[00:30] Samira Gupta: great, yep we'll show prompt sets, baselines, and regression alerts. quick qual question — what's your current hosting? are you running models in house or are you using hosted APIs today?
[00:42] Jordan Reyes: today it's hybrid; prod is on a managed endpoint from a cloud vendor for latency, but we also run a local quantized model for batched offline processing. latency sensitive flows are the API ones.
[00:55] Marcus Lee: timeline wise, we're aiming for a pilot in the next 2–3 weeks and then a broader rollout Q3 if things look good.
[01:05] Samira Gupta: perfect, that aligns with a 1-week pilot. ok I'll share my screen now — let me know if the meeting audio overlaps cause sometimes the auto-transcription picks up two voices.
[01:20] [Screen share started] Samira Gupta: this is the Redwood console — evals tab. on the left you see prompt set groups, we've preloaded a demo set and you can create custom sets per product. here's Silverline's demo set — notice each prompt has tags (triage, summary, PHI-check).
[01:40] Priya Natarajan: small note: when you say PHI-check tag, how is the PII/PHI detection done? is that on our side or via Redwood?
[01:52] Samira Gupta: good q — we have a detector that can run locally in private deployment or as a managed service in hosted. for private/VPC customers most run the detector inside their network, then Redwood's evals accept the labels only — we don't ingest raw PHI for hosted unless customers opt in and it's encrypted via KMS. (transcription: K M S sometimes shows as k m s)
[02:10] Jordan Reyes: ok cool. can you show an A/B comparison where we compare two model versions and a baseline?
[02:20] Samira Gupta: yes — under comparisons we pick model A (our current hosted variant) and model B (a compact quantized variant). the UI shows per-prompt metrics: exact-match, F1 on clinical entities, hallucination rate (heuristic), and a cost/tokens per response. you can run an A/B across a prompt set or across slices — e.g., by diagnosis or prompt length.
[02:44] [00:02:44] Samira Gupta: here's an example where model B has slightly lower hallucination but higher latency because it's on dedicated CPU fallback — the console surfaces that tradeoff and suggests a rollout policy.
[03:00] Jordan Reyes: how are regressions detected? is it threshold-based or statistical?
[03:08] Samira Gupta: both. you can set absolute thresholds per metric (e.g., hallucination < 1%) and also statistical change detection across a moving baseline. if a regression is detected the system can fire an alert, open a ticket, and snapshot the prompt+response for root-cause.
[03:28] Marcus Lee: can those alerts go to our pager/CI? we want failures to block model promotion in our CI pipeline.
[03:36] Samira Gupta: yes — webhook, Slack, email, and direct CI integrations are supported. many customers wire alerts to their CD pipeline so a regression prevents rollout. we have a webhook payload that includes the triggering metric, prompt id, example input/output, and a signed pointer to the artifact (for private customers the pointer is in the VPC object store).
[03:58] Jordan Reyes: signed pointer meaning presigned S3 link?
[04:02] Samira Gupta: exactly, or presigned object store link depending on deployment.
[04:10] [04:10] Alex Morgan: quick check for procurement/security — do you require us to do a private deployment for PHI?
[04:18] Jordan Reyes: for compliance we prefer private or dedicated, but we might evaluate hosted if the SOC 2/contract flow works.
[04:28] Samira Gupta: understood. we can run pilot in our hosted with encrypted at rest and customer-managed keys, or spin up Redwood Private in your VPC if you need full control. for SOC 2 we already provide the report — I'll share that.
[04:42] [05:00] Samira Gupta: now back to demo — here's a prompt set creation flow. you upload examples, label expected output or acceptance heuristic. you can attach evaluators — e.g., tokenized F1 for entities, regex for PHI, and a custom Python-scored evaluator via a sandbox.
[05:20] Jordan Reyes: can we run custom evaluators locally? we have internal clinical scoring logic we don't want to share externally.
[05:28] Samira Gupta: yes — in private or dedicated, the evaluator can run inside your environment and only the metrics are sent to Redwood. the UI will display the metrics but the raw signals stay in your network.
[05:40] Priya Natarajan: network requirements for private — we use strict egress rules, will Redwood need outbound access?
[05:48] Samira Gupta: minimal. for full private deployment, control plane can be either hosted or customer-managed; there are deployment modes where no egress is required except for telemetry if you enable it. we'll capture exact network ports in the architecture doc.
[06:02] [06:02] Samira Gupta: next I'll show regression alert config — you can create a policy, scope by prompt sets, stratify by model version and environment, and pick the trigger (absolute threshold or change over baseline). you can choose sensitivity and set a cooldown so you don't get noisy alerts.
[06:20] Marcus Lee: what's the typical noise level? our team is already overloaded with noisy alerts.
[06:26] Samira Gupta: we provide calibrated defaults and a 'staging' mode that surfaces alerts only to a monitoring Slack channel for 24–72 hours before you push them to ops. also you can combine metrics (e.g., hallucination > 1% AND F1 drop > 5%) to reduce false positives.
[06:44] [06:44] Jordan Reyes: can we do A/B on the same traffic split gradually? for example, 10% traffic to model B and evaluate, then ramp?
[06:52] Samira Gupta: absolutely — the rollout module integrates with routing so you can do canary 10/90, do shadowing, or run discrete A/B experiments. the console will correlate metrics to traffic split and give statistical significance guidance.
[07:06] [07:06] Samira Gupta: here's the evaluation dashboard — table with per-prompt rows and aggregate ribbons. clicking into a row shows examples, the model outputs, evaluator results, and a diff view for A/B where you see model A vs model B side-by-side. note transcription: sometimes model names are mis-heard as g p t four oh but in UI you'll see the canonical model id.
[07:30] Jordan Reyes: can we label prompts as 'blocking' vs 'monitoring'? some prompts should block deployment if they fail.
[07:38] Samira Gupta: yes — tags include blocking/monitoring and you can configure policies to block rollout if any blocking prompt fails. that integrates with our CI webhook.
[07:48] [08:00] Samira Gupta: now for A B comparisons — you can run statistical tests, and the UI will compute confidence intervals and show a recommended winner. it also estimates cost delta per 1M requests based on token distributions.
[08:14] Marcus Lee: cost estimate sounds valuable — does it account for batching and KV cache effects?
[08:20] Samira Gupta: it uses profiler data from the runtime and measured token distributions; for hosted we use observed batching/kv cache lift in similar workloads, for dedicated you can plug in your runtime profiling numbers. it's an estimate but it's usually helpful for decisions.
[08:34] [08:34] Jordan Reyes: security — SSO, RBAC, audit logs?
[08:38] Samira Gupta: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. audit logs are retained per your plan and can be exported to your SIEM. for private we can also forward logs to your central stack.
[08:50] Priya Natarajan: KMS — can we use our HSM?
[08:54] Samira Gupta: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Private and Dedicated. hosted supports customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[09:04] [09:04] Alex Morgan: demo note — we often recommend customers start with hosted evals to get fast feedback, then move critical production traffic to dedicated or private.
[09:12] Jordan Reyes: one more technical: how are hallucination heuristics computed?
[09:18] Samira Gupta: multiple approaches: entity-level divergence, contradiction detection, and reference-based scoring if you have gold outputs. we also run embeddings-similarity checks to surface semantically unrelated content. heuristics are configurable per prompt set.
[09:34] Marcus Lee: do we need to instrument our app to send each prompt response to Redwood or can we batch?
[09:40] Samira Gupta: you can batch — many teams batch nightly for evaluation or stream in production for near real-time monitoring. streaming supports sampling to save cost.
[09:52] Jordan Reyes: does Redwood store the raw prompt/response? we've strict rules about PHI retention.
[09:58] Samira Gupta: for hosted, by default we store artifacts encrypted, retention configurable, and you can opt out of storing raw artifacts — only metrics will be retained. for private deployment you can choose to never leave your network. we'll capture retention settings in the pilot doc.
[10:16] [10:16] Samira Gupta: quick walkthrough of regression alert payload — here's an example webhook, it includes metric name, value, baseline, affected prompt ids and presigned artifact links. we also sign payloads and support mutual TLS for high security customers.
[10:34] Priya Natarajan: mutual TLS is a requirement for us for any automated pushes.
[10:38] Samira Gupta: noted. we support mTLS for webhooks.
[10:44] [11:00] Samira Gupta: next demo piece — historical trend explorer. you can view metric trends over time, segment by model version, prompt tag, and run cohort analyses. this helps triage degraded performance after model rollouts. here's a sample where a baseline shift happened after a tokenizer change.
[11:22] Jordan Reyes: tokenizer change — do you detect tokenization drift automatically?
[11:28] Samira Gupta: yes we track token-level statistics and highlight distributions shifts that can cause performance swings.
[11:36] [11:36] Marcus Lee: about the sandboxed custom evaluators — what's the runtime? can we bring Python libs?
[11:42] Samira Gupta: we provide a secure sandbox. for private/dedicated you can run your evaluator locally with full libs. hosted sandbox supports a curated set of libs; if you need extra packages we can discuss pilot onboarding.
[11:56] Jordan Reyes: for acceptance criteria — we want hallucination under 0.5% on blocking prompts and entity F1 > 92%. can Redwood enforce that during rollout?
[12:08] Samira Gupta: yes — you can configure those thresholds and the policy will block rollout and trigger alerts.
[12:16] [12:16] Alex Morgan: moving to piloting — recommended scope: 200 prompts across 4 slices, run A/B across current hosted model vs a quantized compact variant, monitor for 7 days with daily snapshot reports. thoughts?
[12:32] Jordan Reyes: sounds reasonable. can we include a smoke test that checks for PHI redaction?
[12:38] Samira Gupta: yes — we'll add a PHI redaction check as a blocking evaluator.
[12:44] Priya Natarajan: also we need to agree on data retention and egress.
[12:48] Alex Morgan: Agreed — Samira will send architecture + retention options.
[12:52] [13:00] Samira Gupta: ok last section — integrations and automation. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization profiles to hit cost/latency targets. we also export recommended rollout policies based on historical performance.
[13:16] Marcus Lee: does optimize actually change models or just suggest configs?
[13:20] Samira Gupta: it suggests. changes are applied by your orchestration; we integrate with your CI/CD to automate rollouts if you choose.
[13:28] Jordan Reyes: curious about the unit economics — can we get a projected cost per 1M calls for dedicated vs hosted?
[13:36] Alex Morgan: yes we'll include that in the pricing deck — it's part of the pilot proposal.
[13:42] [14:00] Jordan Reyes: Any limitations on prompt set size or eval throughput?
[14:06] Samira Gupta: not really — for large-scale evals we recommend dedicated capacity or offline batch runs. the console handles millions of rows but runtime depends on your infra.
[14:18] [14:18] Marcus Lee: how do you handle model failover in production? say the hosted model fails and we need to fallback to an older version.
[14:26] Samira Gupta: smart routing supports fallback policies by model variant, region, and capacity tier. you can prioritize lower-cost variants or older stable models when a regression is detected.
[14:36] Jordan Reyes: about metrics export — can we send metrics to Prometheus or DataDog?
[14:42] Samira Gupta: yes we support metric sinks and exporters; alerts can also be forwarded.
[14:48] [15:00] Alex Morgan: let's surface any objections — Jordan?
[15:04] Jordan Reyes: main concerns: PHI handling, alert noise, and how much engineering work to integrate.
[15:12] Samira Gupta: all valid — we'll scope pilot to minimize engineering: a small ingestion shim, pre-built webhook for CI, and a few blocking evaluators.
[15:22] Priya Natarajan: what's the expected token overhead for evals? we don't want to double spend tokens for monitoring.
[15:30] Samira Gupta: you can sample. for streaming you can send 5–10% of traffic or batch nightly to limit cost. Optimize will also recommend caching/prefixing that can reduce token overhead.
[15:44] [16:00] Samira Gupta: demo wrap-up — I'll send the pilot doc after the call. Alex will follow up on pricing. Jordan can share the sample prompts.
[16:12] Jordan Reyes: ok we'll get the prompts to you.
[16:18] Marcus Lee: one more thing — we occasionally do human-in-the-loop labeling, can Redwood hook into that workflow?
[16:24] Samira Gupta: yes — we have a labeling integration and you can export failed examples to a labeling queue.
[16:32] [16:32] Alex Morgan: going to do a quick recap and next steps.
[16:36] Alex Morgan: recap: pilot scope 200 prompts, 7-day A/B, blocking evaluators for PHI and entity F1, alerts wired to CI and Slack, deliver SOC2 and arch diagrams, pricing + cost projection. next steps: Alex send pilot proposal by 5/30; Samira send SOC2 & deployment doc; Jordan provide prompts by 5/30; Priya confirm network/KMS constraints by 6/01.
[16:58] Jordan Reyes: sounds good.
[17:04] [56:54] Speaker 3: thanks everyone, bye.
[56:58] Alex Morgan: thanks all, talk soon.
